s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of neurological symptoms with headache, nausea, vomiting, ataxia, diplopia, and altered mental status, with evidence of demyelination on imaging
salient_findings: Initial presentation with headache, nausea, and vomiting
Development of ataxia, diplopia, and recurrence of headache
Abnormal T2-weighted MRI findings with increased signaling in multiple brain and spinal cord regions
Elevated opening pressure on lumbar puncture
Progressive neurological deterioration with decreased sensorium, hallucinations, and gait disturbance
key_facts: 48-year-old woman with no prior health issues
5-day history of headache, nausea, and vomiting
Initial physical examination and laboratory tests were normal
Diagnosed with tension headache and sinusitis initially
Treated with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and proton pump inhibitor
Developed ataxia, diplopia, and recurrence of headache
T2-weighted MRI showed increased signaling in left temporal lobe, bilateral pontine regions, left peridentate nucleus, and cervical spinal cord
Elevated blood pressure, serum sodium, glucose, and white-cell count during hospitalization
Neurological symptoms included decreased sensorium, hallucinations, diminished attention span, and gait disturbance
Lumbar puncture showed elevated opening pressure
Received plasmapheresis without improvement
Follow-up T2-weighted MRI showed progressive enlargement of bilateral pontine regions with hydrocephalus and mass effect on the fourth ventricle

shortlist.label: Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute onset of neurological symptoms with evidence of demyelination on imaging

shortlist.label: Acute Demyelinating Encephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical suspicion for demyelinating process with radiographic and laboratory findings

shortlist.label: Infectious Encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated white-cell count and clinical presentation of encephalitis

shortlist.label: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Altered mental status and neurological symptoms with potential for autoimmune etiology

shortlist.label: Multiple Sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Demyelination on imaging and subacute onset of neurological symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms and MRI findings, including increased signaling in the left temporal lobe, bilateral pontine regions, left peridentate nucleus, and cervical spinal cord, are consistent with an acute demyelinating process, and the diagnosis of acute demyelinating encephalopathy was made based on radiographic, laboratory, and clinical findings

rejected.label: Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis
rejected.why: While similar to acute demyelinating encephalopathy, the lack of clear post-infectious or post-vaccination context makes this less likely

rejected.label: Infectious Encephalitis
rejected.why: The absence of pathological enhancement of the pons and the progression of symptoms despite treatment suggest a non-infectious cause

rejected.label: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis
rejected.why: There is no mention of specific antibodies or teratoma, which are commonly associated with this condition

rejected.label: Multiple Sclerosis
rejected.why: The rapid progression and severity of symptoms, as well as the lack of prior episodes, make this diagnosis less likely
